label: Terminal Doc
review:
- This video is a Terminal Doc, a dark typographic documentary where the text is the picture, and the following are its intended, approved look: a near-black canvas, mostly empty; sparse monospace capitals in white and grey; letters that lift out of a word and arc into a new order; a string flying into a corner-bracket box labelled with an operation (HASH, BASE64) and coming out as another string; numbers that resolve out of flickering glyph noise, right to left; a faint grey wall of ciphertext behind the stage; a typed command line with a block caret; a stream of guesses racing through one slot until one locks; thin bracket lines under a string with a short label, and a quoted source with a [n] citation below; at most one red or blue glowing element at a time; long held beats with something small changing every few seconds; hard cuts between beats, sometimes a CRT-off collapse to a line. A video may use the amber CRT skin instead: amber pixel lettering, scanlines, a dark vignette and a soft glow on every glyph. Captions are a terminal log strip: a LOG label and a running clock over a hairline, monospace capitals typed on word by word behind a prompt, the word being spoken in red (amber in the CRT skin) with a block caret. Do NOT report the on-screen text, the typing, the noise glyphs, the ciphertext wall, the empty frame or the lack of pictures as defects, and do not suggest adding images, icons, people, colour or texture: they are the style.
- Do report: text cut off at the frame edge or running into other text, a bracket or label over a string, text too small to read on a phone, a glow on a string the narration is not talking about at that moment, a value shown wrong (a hash, a count, a number that does not match what is said), stage text that repeats the sentence being spoken instead of showing the thing it is about, and a stretch of more than about three seconds where nothing on screen changes.
script:
Every beat's `visual` is a **text** brief: the one string, number or quoted source on stage and what happens to it (`"SUNSHINE flies into a HASH box and comes out as a hex digest"`, `"the keyspace 208,827,064,576 resolves out of noise"`). The video is typography throughout, so a role ("an attacker", "the server") is never drawn: it is named in the narration while the stage shows the string it acts on.

The narration is a sober documentary voice over a mostly empty dark frame. Name the exact string, key, hash, number or date the viewer should watch, because it becomes the picture: "the word SUNSHINE", "two hundred and eight billion", "in 1990". Give each sentence one transformation (a word is hashed, letters are swapped, a number is counted) and give a number its own sentence when it is the punchline. When a claim needs a source, say where it comes from ("a 2023 benchmark"), because it becomes a bracket note with a citation. Never write a beat that needs a person, a place or a photograph: this style has none.

picture.opening: Beat 1 has the string or number the first sentence names already changing at frame 0: typing, resolving out of noise or flying into a box, over the ciphertext wall. Never an empty screen waiting for its first line.
picture.turn: A new beat on the first word of a turn or a re-opening (a collapse cut where the subject changes), or a push, a bracket or a wall change in the current beat at that moment.
picture.payoff: The answer as the largest thing on stage (size xl), with a push in and the one glow.
picture.ending: Hold the payoff beat to the last frame. No sign-off line and no clear at the end.

best_for: a string, key or number transformed step by step (encoded, encrypted, hashed, scrambled)
what a computer does with text and numbers under the hood
computing history told through one command, message or number
avoid_for: components passing requests, packets or messages between each other (System Flow draws those)
arithmetic or reasoning worked out step by step by hand (Whiteboard fits it)
real, named things the viewer came to see as pictures (Motion Graphics)
lists of everyday habits or behaviours one person reacts to (Bean Explainer)
people's life stories and characters the viewer must recognise
signals: the script turns on one word, password, key, hash or string
something is encoded, encrypted or transformed letter by letter
one large number is the punchline (a keyspace, a count, a time to crack)
the script quotes a source, a message or a date as evidence
a command typed at a terminal and what it prints

house.label: near-black, white and grey monospace, red and blue glow

crt.label: amber CRT phosphor: pixel lettering, scanlines, vignette

moves.word: a string appears in a slot (scramble, type or cut)
moves.rearrange: the letters of one string lift and arc into another string
moves.encode: a string flies into a labelled box and comes out as another string
moves.number: a number resolves out of glyph noise right to left, or counts up
moves.wall: the grey ciphertext wall behind the stage: level 0 off, 1 faint, 2 bright
moves.grid: an alphabet or table builds row by row across the whole stage
moves.stream: guesses race through a slot and lock on the target string
moves.bracket: a hairline bracket under an element with a short label, and an optional quoted note with a citation
moves.glow: one element (or one row or span of it) turns red or blue and blooms
moves.type: a command typed behind a $ prompt, with up to three output lines
moves.push: a slow push-in over a held beat
moves.custom: a move the agent wrote for this video
